title.en: Ghost of far-right paramilitaries hovers over Colombia’s presidential runoff vote
title.zh: 哥伦比亚总统决选笼罩在极右翼准军事组织的阴影之下

summary.en: Colombians are preparing for a presidential runoff election between two candidates with vastly different personal histories shaped by militias and opposing visions for the country. The election takes place under the lingering influence of far-right paramilitaries.
summary.zh: 哥伦比亚人正准备进行总统决选，两位候选人的个人经历都深受民兵组织影响，对国家抱持截然不同的愿景。此次选举在极右翼准军事组织的阴影下进行。

body.en: Colombians will choose on Sunday between two men whose lives have been very differently shaped by the militias, and whose visions for the country are poles apart Whoever wins Sunday’s presidential runoff vote in Colombia, the country’s next leader will have a personal history intertwined with one of the criminal forces at the heart of a decades-long armed conflict that claimed nearly half a million lives. The lives of Iván Cepeda and Abelardo de la Espriella have, in very different ways, been shaped by their relationship with Colombia’s paramilitaries – private armies originally established by rightwing landowners, drug traffickers, businessmen, mining magnates and politicians to fight leftwing guerrilla groups. Continue reading...
body.zh: 周日，哥伦比亚人将在两名男子中做出选择，他们的生活因民兵的影响截然不同，他们对国家的愿景也截然不同。无论谁赢得周日哥伦比亚总统决选，该国的下一任领导人都将与处于长达数十年武装冲突核心的犯罪势力交织在一起，这场武装冲突夺走了近50万人的生命。伊万·塞佩达（Iván Cepeda）和阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉（Abelardo de la Espriella）的生活以截然不同的方式受到他们与哥伦比亚准军事部队的关系的影响。准军事部队最初是由右翼地主、毒贩、商人、矿业巨头和政客建立的，旨在打击左翼游击队组织。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As Colombia faces a pivotal election, the deep divisions and the lingering "ghost" of past violence remind us that societal struggles often run deeper than political contests. Yahweh's Word encourages us to recognize that true battles are often against unseen forces that perpetuate division and injustice, calling for a perspective beyond mere human...
reflection.zh: 哥伦比亚面临关键选举之际，深刻的分歧和过去暴力的“幽灵”提醒我们，社会斗争往往比政治竞争更为深远。雅伟的话语鼓励我们认识到，真正的争战常常是针对那些使分裂和不公持续存在的无形势力，呼吁我们超越单纯的人际对立来看待问题。

verse.textEn: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.
verse.textZh: 因我们并不是与属血气的争战，乃是与那些执政的、掌权的、管辖这幽暗世界的，以及天空属灵气的恶魔争战。

title.en: Key Trump allies and Musk on leaked list for secretive Peter Thiel retreat

The annual Dialog retreats, which have been compared to other quasi-secret elite conferences like the Bilderberg Group and Bohemian Grove since they began in 2006, have had some participants revealed in previous media reports. Fairly little is known about the invitation-only event, which is usually held at luxury establishments around the world and features organized discussions on global affairs. Continue reading...

Yahweh reminds us that knowing the truth can ultimately set us free, bringing...

title.en: Steve Rosenberg: Moscow oil refinery attack brings Russia's war with Ukraine closer to home
title.zh: 莫斯科炼油厂遇袭，俄乌战争离家园更近

summary.en: An attack on a Moscow oil refinery has brought Russia's war with Ukraine closer to the Russian capital, disrupting the sense of normalcy for residents.
summary.zh: 莫斯科一家炼油厂遭到袭击，使俄罗斯与乌克兰的战争离俄罗斯首都更近，打破了当地居民的正常生活感。

body.en:
There are moments when life in Moscow feels completely normal. Thursday morning wasn't one of them.

In the south-east of the city an oil refinery had been hit during a Ukrainian drone attack - even from a distance the sight was surreal.

Thick smoke billowing from the direction of the facility had turned the sky dark. Like a giant black shroud, it hung over the Moscow skyline.

As extraordinary and eye-catching this was, so was the reaction of people near the refinery.

Paying minimal attention to the huge clouds of smoke, an angler sat by the side of a pond, staring out across the water as he carried on fishing.

Shoppers were heading to and from a supermarket, as if this was just another Thursday.

I realised then that my sense of what's normal in Moscow and what's not, needed updating.

For so long, the war on Ukraine felt very distant to people in the Russian capital. Many pretended it wasn't happening at all, but that's harder to do as the front line creeps closer to the city.

Over the past year-and-a-half, Muscovites have woken to news that army generals in Moscow have been assassinated, and drones have been targeting the capital.

Thursday's attack was one of the largest aerial assaults on the Moscow region since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

As well as damage to the oil refinery, shopping centres and residential buildings were hit, too. According to the governor of the Moscow region, an eight-year-old girl was killed in a fire caused by one of the drone strikes.

"I'm not totally surprised by what happened," says Slava, who lives in an apartment block opposite the oil refinery. "But I didn't expect such a big attack."

"I heard explosions and saw lots of smoke. It's the kind of thing you normally see in the movies. I saw it from my apartment window."

"It took us four years to win World War Two, even though our soldiers had little food and water," she told me.

How do the Russian authorities respond to people like Nadezhda, to Russians struggling to understand why the Kremlin's so-called "special military operation" is taking so long, and how it can be that the war has come to their city?

Russian officials regularly accuse the West of prolonging the war in Ukraine, blaming European leaders and Nato for supporting Kyiv.

But on Thursday, President Vladimir Putin said nothing about the drone assault. The news bulletins on Russian TV channels barely mentioned it.

When Russian newspapers reported the story the following day, I detected a common thread in their coverage: a coordinated message, perhaps, for the domestic audience.

It can be summed up as this: "However bad it is for us, Ukraine's suffering more".

"Our attacks are doing far more damage to Ukraine than Ukraine is doing to us," declared the ultra-pro-Kremlin...
body.zh: 有时候，莫斯科的生活感觉完全正常。星期四早上不是其中之一。 在该市东南部，一家炼油厂在乌克兰无人机袭击中遭到袭击——即使从远处看，这种景象也是超现实的。 从设施方向冒出的滚滚浓烟使天空变得漆黑。它就像一块巨大的黑色裹尸布，悬挂在莫斯科的天际线上。 这件事非同寻常、引人注目，炼油厂附近人们的反应也是如此。 一名钓鱼者坐在池塘边，一边钓鱼，一边对巨大的烟雾毫不在意。 购物者们往返于超市，仿佛这只是又一个星期四。 然后我意识到我对莫斯科正常和不正常的认识需要更新。 长期以来，俄罗斯首都的人们对乌克兰战争感到非常遥远。许多人假装这一切根本没有发生，但随着前线越来越接近城市，这变得更难了。 在过去的一年半里，莫斯科人一觉醒来就得知莫斯科陆军将领被暗杀、无人机瞄准首都的消息。 周四的袭击是自俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以来莫斯科地区最大规模的空袭之一。 除了炼油厂受损之外，购物中心和住宅楼也受到了影响。据莫斯科地区州长称，一名八岁女孩在一次无人机袭击引发的火灾中丧生。 “我对所发生的事情并不完全感到惊讶，”住在炼油厂对面公寓楼的斯拉瓦说。 “但没想到攻击这么大。” “我听到了爆炸声，看到了很多烟雾。这是你通常在电影中看到的那种东西。我从我公寓的窗户看到了它。” “我们花了四年时间才赢得了第二次世界大战，尽管我们的士兵几乎没有食物和水，”她告诉我。 俄罗斯当局如何回应像娜杰日达这样的人，以及俄罗斯人如何努力理解为什么克里姆林宫所谓的“特别军事行动”花了这么长时间，以及战争怎么会降临到他们的城市？ 俄罗斯官员经常指责西方国家延长乌克兰战争，指责欧洲领导人和北约支持基辅。 但周四，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京对无人机袭击事件只字不提。俄罗斯电视频道的新闻报道几乎没有提及此事。 当俄罗斯报纸第二天报道这个故事时，我在他们的报道中发现了一个共同点：也许是针对国内观众的协调一致的信息。 可以概括为：“无论对我们来说有多糟糕，乌克兰遭受的苦难更多”。 极端亲克里姆林宫宣称：“我们的袭击对乌克兰造成的损害远远超过乌克兰对我们造成的损害。”

Yahweh's word reminds us that those who live by the sword often experience its destructive power firsthand, bringing the consequences of conflict to unexpected places. This serves as a somber reminder of the far-reaching and often...
reflection.zh: 莫斯科一家炼油厂遇袭的消息，凸显了暴力往往会回到其源头的痛苦现实。雅伟的话语提醒我们，那些仗剑而生的人，往往会亲身经历其毁灭性的力量，将冲突的后果带到意想不到的地方。这沉重地提醒我们，战争的性质往往是深远且相互作用的。

title.en: One killed and dozens hurt in train collision north of London
title.zh: 伦敦北部火车相撞造成一人死亡、数十人受伤

summary.en: A video posted on social media showed what appeared to be the front of one train entangled with the back of another.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A train driver has died and dozens more injured in a collision between two commuter services in London on Friday.

Both trains were travelling south to London St Pancras station on Friday afternoon when they collided outside the town of Bedford, about 100km north of London. The trains were travelling from Corby and Nottingham respectively.

East Midlands Railway, which operated both London-bound trains involved in the crash, confirmed in a statement on X on Saturday that the driver of one of the services had been killed. The company had cancelled all trains to and from St Pancras for the rest of Friday and was unable to confirm the schedule for Saturday.

A video posted on social media by one of the passengers showed what appeared to be the front of one train entangled with the back of another, with the carriages appearing to remain upright on the tracks.

The East of England Ambulance Service said that in addition to a person who died at the scene, 11 people suffered very serious injuries, 22 were seriously injured and 56 had minor injuries.

"My thoughts are with the family of the person who has sadly lost their life, and with those who have been seriously injured," Prime Minister Keir Starmer said in a statement.

The cause of the incident was not immediately known, and transport minister Heidi Alexander said an investigation was underway.

Peter Knapp, a doctor who said on social media site Bluesky he was on board one of the trains, described a "sudden crash" with one carriage off the rails and said he had sustained minor injuries.

"There was a moment of being flung into the chair in front, and then I saw smoke," Knapp said.

"I got up and I saw a lot of people who were unable to speak, had broken legs," he said.

"And then I managed to get out of the train and because I'm quite thin I was able to squeeze out through the gap in the doors."

Various posts on social media showed dozens of people, some with bandages but many who appeared uninjured, standing and sitting among emergency vehicles parked on a road that runs parallel to the train tracks.

The RMT union, which represents many railway workers, said it was monitoring the situation and expressed its concern over reports of "serious injuries" suffered by both train staff and passengers.

title.en: Israel and Hezbollah continue strikes despite ceasefire agreement

body.en:
At least a dozen people have reportedly been killed by Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon, less than 24 hours after a new ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah was announced.

Officials in the Nabatieh district said attacks had killed 16 people and injured at least a dozen more, after Israeli warplanes, drones, and artillery targeted numerous areas.

The Israeli military said it struck "Hezbollah terrorist targets" after the group fired over 50 projectiles at Israeli forces in the region.

Washington has criticised Israel's ongoing operations in Lebanon, which was drawn into the US-Iran war when Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for a strike that killed Iran's supreme leader.

Washington also fears that the continuing tensions between Israel and Lebanon could undermine the US peace deal with Iran , which includes a commitment to end fighting on "all fronts" including Lebanon.

US envoy, Steve Witkoff, is reported to be heading to Switzerland for initial talks with Iran to help cement the agreement.

While it may have helped prevent a wider regional escalation for the time being, the deal leaves unresolved the central disputes at the heart of the conflict, including Israel's military presence in southern Lebanon and the future of Hezbollah's weapons.

A Hezbollah official told the BBC it does not recognise the ceasefire that was announced by US officials on Friday afternoon, and it rejects the Israeli objective to operate freely inside Lebanon.

Senior Hezbollah official Hassan Fadlallah said his group had the right to respond to Israeli attacks.

"What concerns us is that the enemy fully and comprehensively respects the ceasefire, and doesn't attempt to attack our country and villages or seek to occupy any new position," he said, as quoted in Lebanon's state-run National News Agency (NNA).

Previous ceasefires between Israel and Hezbollah have still seen near-daily cross-border strikes, with both sides accusing each other of violating the agreement.

Before Friday's ceasefire was announced, Israel said it had no intention of withdrawing its forces from Lebanon and had insisted that its conflict with Hezbollah was separate from the war on Iran.

Earlier on Friday Lebanon's health ministry said 47 people were killed and 97 wounded in Israeli air strikes, while the Israeli military said four of its soldiers were also killed.

Ali, a Red Cross first responder in Nabatieh, told the BBC that it was "the most intense night" he can remember.

Those strikes came a day after the US and Iranian presidents signed an initial peace deal aiming to end the war, including in Lebanon, with immediate effect, but strikes continued.

title.en: Bolivia declares state of emergency over blockade crisis

summary.en: The crisis in Bolivia have worsened since April as roadblocks and demonstrations crippled the nation.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Bolivia's military is poised to crack down on protesters after President Rodrigo Paz declared a state of emergency following weeks of crippling blockades.

The state of emergency will enable wider military deployment to clear blockades and restore order after protests brought the economy to a halt in the past 50 days.

The emergency declaration on Saturday gives Paz broader constitutional tools to restore order, such as sending armed forces to clear blockades, which have been intensifying since April.

While the order goes into effect immediately, the president must notify Congress of the state of emergency within 24 hours ‌of issuing the ‌decree, which then ⁠has up to 72 hours to approve or reject the measure.

Protesting groups, many allied to former leftist president Evo Morales, have cut off key roads, stranding trucks and choking supplies of food, fuel and medicines to many areas, including La Paz.

The conflict initially erupted after Paz abruptly cut longstanding fuel subsidies to shrink the deficit amid a worsening dollar crunch and talks with the International Monetary Fund.

Despite later steps to stabilise fuel ⁠prices and reverse unpopular land reforms, protests intensified into broader discontent, with ‌unions demanding wage increases, an end to fuel and dollar shortages, and Paz's resignation.

Paz's declaration came in a live message to the ‌nation just hours after he unveiled a deal struck on Friday with the main union, the Bolivian Workers Confederation, that aimed to ease tension.

However, many roads connecting the South American nation's main production centre are under the control of rural associations aligned with Morales, who were not a part of the negotiations and are continuing to protest mainly in the area of Cochabamba.

Paz said the crisis had evolved into an organised attempt to destabilise ‌democracy after weeks of violence and blockades.

He said the state of emergency aims to restore order, protect citizens and ensure the flow of essential goods, while warning that those continuing disruptions would face legal consequences.

"This is not a state of emergency to restrict people's lives ... It is a state of emergency to give freedom back to the people, to free Bolivia from those who use political conflict to block roads and harm the population," Paz said.

title.en: Tourist dies in Dominican Republic luxury resort fire
title.zh: 游客在多米尼加共和国豪华度假村火灾中丧生

summary.en: Nearly 1,700 people were evacuated from the huge blaze at Viva Wyndham Dominicus Beach in Bayahibe, a popular resort town on the Caribbean coast.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A huge fire at a luxury beach resort in the Dominican Republic killed one woman and forced nearly 1,700 guests to be evacuated on Friday.

The woman was a 46-year old Italian tourist, the DAEH emergency services said in a statement to local media. It added that three people were taken to medical facilities and six others were treated on site.

Drone footage shows how widespread the fire was, with buildings spanning the Viva Wyndham Dominicus Beach in the town of Bayahibe on fire, and thick black smoke billowing into the air.

The cause of the early-morning blaze is not yet known, but an initial investigation found the flames spread quickly due to wind conditions and the flammable thatched roofs on some buildings.

The country's Emergency Operations Center (COE) said the fire had been brought under control and guests had been moved to other hotels.

It added that tourist activities in the town and surrounding area were not affected.

Italian news agency Ansa reported that the Italian ambassador to the Dominican Republic met the deceased woman's husband at the hospital. The embassy is helping around 285 Italian tourists who were staying at the resort or nearby, issuing emergency passports to those whose travel documents were destroyed in the fire and arranging flights home.

Bayahibe, a popular resort town on the Caribbean coast, is known for its clear blue waters and sandy beaches.

Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, which franchises about 8,400 hotels around the world, has been contacted for comment.

summary.en: A large fire at a four-star beach resort in the Dominican Republic resulted in the death of one woman and the evacuation of approximately 1,700 tourists. Most of the hotel appeared to be destroyed by the blaze.
summary.zh: 多米尼加共和国一家四星级海滨度假酒店发生大火，造成一名女子死亡，约1,700名游客被疏散。大火似乎摧毁了酒店的大部分区域。

body.en:
A huge fire tore through a four-star beach resort in the Dominican Republic, killing one woman. About 1,700 tourists were evacuated as the fire appeared to destroy most of the hotel.

A woman was killed and almost 1,700 people had to flee after a massive fire broke out at a luxury resort in the Dominican Republic  on Friday, authorities said.

The incident occurred at the Viva Wyndham Dominicus Beach Hotel in Bayahibe, located on the Caribbean nation's southeastern coast.

Fire officials tamed the blaze and an investigation is underway to determine its cause.

An Italian woman — identified as 46-year-old Francesca Valentino — died in the blaze, the DAEH emergency service said in a statement.

It added that three people had been taken to medical facilities and six others were receiving treatment on the site.

According to authorities, the fire forced some 1,690 tourists to be evacuated from the resort to other hotels and nearby establishments.

The flames almost completely devoured the hotel in the resort town, which is popular among international tourists .

The country's Emergency Operations Center said that initial observations indicated the "fire spread rapidly" because the resort's roof was made of thatch and due to wind conditions.

Drone footage being circulated in the local media showed plumes of dark smoke gushing out above the white sand coastline as fires burnt over multiple straw roof structures in the complex.

title.en: After Trump's makeover, the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is now green — with algae
title.zh: 特朗普改造后，林肯纪念堂倒影池变绿——长满藻类

summary.en: A recent patriotic renovation of the historic Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has resulted in the pool turning green with algae, indicating a significant failure in the project.
summary.zh: 林肯纪念堂历史悠久的倒影池在经过一次爱国主义改造后，如今却因藻类滋生而变成绿色，这表明该项目遭遇了重大失败。

body.en:
Strips of "American-flag blue" paint are rising from the bottom of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, videos circulating online appear to show, in the latest disaster to hit its botched $14.6 million ($20.8M) refurbishment.

The Reflecting Pool, which civil rights activist Martin Luther King Jr. looked over as he gave his famous "I have a dream" speech, has undergone a makeover at the direction of Donald Trump to commemorate the country's 250th birthday on 4 July this year.

In May, the pool was drained and a commercial-grade sealant was reportedly added to its granite bottom.

The Virginia-based Atlantic Industrial Coatings company was awarded a controversial US$13.1 million ($18.7M) no-bid contract for the job after having previously worked on one of Trump's golf courses.

"We did a hell of a job," Trump told reporters at the White House last week upon completion, claiming just US$10 million had been spent.

Company owner Eddie Wood confirmed in an email to US publication NBC that the cost had, in fact, blown out.

"But everybody’s looking at that Reflecting Pool," Trump continued. "They can’t believe it reflects. We used a dark blue, it’s called American flag blue."

However, visitors to the iconic Washington site have noticed that the water has turned a distinct shade of green.

Wayne Sobey, environmental consultant at Algae Control Australia, told SBS News that "shallow, flat, non‑circulating pools" like the Lincoln Memorial's create "almost perfect conditions for algal growth," something the administration is continuing to deny is a problem.

Here's how the colour of the Lincoln Reflecting Pool became the latest political flashpoint in a politically charged United States.

Trump's desired overhaul of the Reflecting Pool is part of an ongoing administration push to "beautify" American cities, and its capital in particular, following what it sees as years of Democrat neglect.

Such projects in Washington DC include the complete knock-down and rebuild of the East Wing of the White House, the plans to build a towering victory arch in Washington that will exceed the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, and a US$7.5 million plan to paint the Eisenhower building.

The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is a 619 by 51 metre rectangular pool built in 1922 between the Washington Monument and the Lincoln Memorial.

While it draws millions of tourists each year, it has long had issues with water clarity. It's 6.75 million gallons of still water see blooms of the photosynthetic organism each summer, something Barack Obama spent US$34 million to fix — unsuccessfully.

title.en: Australia confirms first case of H5N1 bird flu as virus reaches every continent
title.zh: 澳大利亚确认首例H5N1禽流感病例，病毒已蔓延至各大洲

summary.en: Australia has reported its first case of the H5N1 bird flu strain, making it the final continent where the virus has now been detected.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚已确认首例H5N1禽流感病例，至此该病毒株已蔓延至全球各大洲。

body.en:
The H5N1 strain of bird flu has for the first time been found in Australia, the country's agriculture ministry confirmed. It means the highly contagious variant has now reached every continent.

The disease was found in a migratory seabird, a brown skua, in remote Western Australia, Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said on Saturday.

The bird was found on a beach at the Cape Le Grand National Park near the town of Esperance, about 700km (434 mi) south-east of Perth, according to local media.

Australia was previously the only continent where the H5N1 bird flu strain had not been found.

The strain can spread quickly among poultry and wild bird populations. Human cases tied to the disease remain uncommon.

"We all knew we couldn't be bird flu-free forever," Collins told a press conference.

Collins added that there was a second suspected case of bird flu - a southern petrel that was found exhausted on an Esperance beach, though she added that there was no "evidence of mass mortalities at this time".

Threatened Species Commissioner Fiona Fraser said authorities would know "within a few days" if the virus was present in any other animal populations in Australia, according to a report by the national broadcaster, the ABC.

The report also quoted the country's Chief Veterinary Officer Beth Cookson who said authorities had been "preparing for this event for a long time" and that the committee for emergency animal disease had convened on Saturday.

The H5N1 strain of bird flu was detected on the remote Australian territories of Heard and McDonald Islands in October last year - located in the southern Indian Ocean.

A study released this week estimated that around 13,000 baby seals from a group of 17,000 on Heard Island were killed by the H5N1 strain of bird flu since last August, more than 75% of the entire group. They also found higher than expected deaths in penguin populations.

Scientists believe bird flu was likely introduced to the islands last August from migrating birds from the French-owned Crozet Islands, about 1,800 km away.

Bird flu is a disease caused by a virus that infects birds and sometimes other animals, such as foxes, seals and otters.

The major strain - circulating among wild birds worldwide - is a type of the virus known as H5N1. It emerged in China in the late 1990s.

Bird migration has led to outbreaks in domestic and wild birds- and in very rare cases also infected humans, usually from contact with sick animals.
body.zh: 澳大利亚农业部证实，澳大利亚首次发现H5N1禽流感病毒株。这意味着这种具有高度传染性的变种现已传播到各大洲。 农业部长朱莉·柯林斯周六表示，这种疾病是在西澳大利亚偏远地区的一种迁徙海鸟棕色贼鸥身上发现的。 据当地媒体报道，这只鸟是在珀斯东南约 700 公里（434 英里）处埃斯佩兰斯镇附近的大角国家公园的海滩上发现的。 澳大利亚此前是唯一未发现H5N1禽流感病毒的大陆。 该菌株可以在家禽和野鸟种群中迅速传播。与该疾病相关的人类病例仍然不常见。 柯林斯在新闻发布会上说：“我们都知道我们不可能永远没有禽流感。” 柯林斯补充说，出现了第二起疑似禽流感病例——一只在埃斯佩兰斯海滩上被发现精疲力尽的南方海燕，不过她补充说，“目前没有大规模死亡的证据”。 据国家广播公司美国广播公司 (ABC) 报道，濒危物种专员菲奥娜·弗雷泽 (Fiona Fraser) 表示，当局将在“几天内”知道澳大利亚任何其他动物种群中是否存在该病毒。 报道还援引该国首席兽医官贝丝·库克森的话说，当局“为这一事件准备了很长时间”，紧急动物疾病委员会已于周六召开会议。 去年10月，在位于南印度洋的赫德岛和麦克唐纳岛的偏远澳大利亚领土上发现了H5N1禽流感病毒株。 本周发布的一项研究估计，自去年 8 月以来，赫德岛 17,000 只小海豹中约有 13,000 只小海豹死于 H5N1 禽流感病毒，占整个海豹种群的 75% 以上。他们还发现企鹅种群的死亡人数高于预期。 科学家认为，禽流感很可能是去年 8 月由来自法属克罗泽群岛（距离约 1,800 公里）的候鸟传入这些岛屿的。 禽流感是一种由病毒引起的疾病，它会感染鸟类，有时还会感染其他动物，如狐狸、海豹和水獭。 在全世界野生鸟类中传播的主要毒株是一种名为 H5N1 的病毒。它于20世纪90年代末在中国出现。 鸟类迁徙导​​致家禽和野生鸟类爆发疫情，在极少数情况下，人类也受到感染，通常是通过接触患病动物。

reflection.en: The global spread of H5N1 bird flu, now reaching every continent, reminds us to observe the natural world closely. Yahweh's creation, including its animals and birds, often reveals profound truths about our interconnectedness and the challenges we face. Understanding these patterns can guide our response to such widespread biological events.
reflection.zh: H5N1禽流感蔓延至全球各大洲，包括澳大利亚，提醒我们要仔细观察自然界。雅伟的创造，包括其中的动物和鸟类，常常揭示我们相互关联的深刻真理以及我们面临的挑战。理解这些模式可以指导我们应对此类广泛的生物事件。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: First case of H5 bird flu confirmed in Australia
title.zh: 澳大利亚确诊首例H5禽流感病例

summary.en: A migratory sea bird in Western Australia has tested positive for the contagious H5 variant of bird flu, marking the first detected case of this strain on the continent. Australia had previously been the only continent without a confirmed detection of the H5 bird flu strain.
summary.zh: 西澳大利亚州的一只候鸟被检测出H5型高致病性禽流感病毒呈阳性，这是该毒株首次在澳大利亚大陆被发现。此前，澳大利亚是唯一没有检测到该毒株的洲。

body.en:
A migratory seabird tested positive for the contagious H5 variant of avian influenza in Western Australia. Australia had been the only continent where H5 was not detected.

On Saturday,  Australia confirmed its first mainland case of the deadly H5 strain of bird flu .

The disease was detected in a migratory seabird — a brown skua — in a remote part ‌of ⁠Western Australia, Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said at a press briefing in Canberra.

The development means that the highly contagious variant of avian influenza is now present on every continent.

The bird was found near a beach at the Cape Le Grand National Park, about ​700 ‌kilometers (430 miles) from Western Australia's capital, Perth.

"Whilst disappointing, this is not unexpected, given the global spread of the H5 bird flu," Collins said.

"I can confirm there is still no evidence of any mass mortalities at this time, nor is there any evidence of infection in any poultry," she said.

The H5 strain has led to high death rates in poultry and wild birds throughout the planet.

It has also affected mammals, with detections in animals like cats, goats, alpacas and pigs.

Australia had been gearing up for the variant's arrival with stricter biosecurity at farms, testing of shore birds and vaccinations among species that were vulnerable.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said that the detection of the case was concerning, adding that his government would undertake steps to curb the spread of the disease.

"This is something that has happened through migratory birds, and has happened by definition around the world, and this is why we are preparing for this," he said.

body.zh: 在西澳大利亚，一只候鸟海鸟的传染性 H5 型禽流感病毒检测呈阳性。迄今为止，澳大利亚是唯一尚未发现该菌株的大陆。 澳大利亚周六证实了大陆首例致命 H5 禽流感病例。 农业部长朱莉·柯林斯在堪培拉举行的新闻发布会上表示，在西澳大利亚偏远地区的一种迁徙海鸟——棕色贼鸥中发现了这种疾病。 这一进展意味着高度传染性的禽流感变种现已存在于各大洲。 这只鸟是在勒格兰德角国家公园的海滩附近发现的，距离西澳大利亚州首府珀斯约 700 公里（430 英里）。 柯林斯说：“虽然令人失望，但鉴于 H5 禽流感在全球蔓延，这并不意外。” 她说：“我可以确认，目前还没有任何大规模死亡的证据，也没有任何家禽感染的证据。” H5 毒株导致全球家禽和野鸟的高死亡率。 它还影响了哺乳动物，在猫、山羊、羊驼和猪等动物中都检测到了这种病毒。 澳大利亚一直在为该变种的到来做好准备，在农场采取更严格的生物安全措施，对滨鸟进行测试，并对脆弱物种进行疫苗接种。 总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞表示，该病例的发现令人担忧，并补充说，他的政府将采取措施遏制该疾病的传播。 他说：“这是通过候鸟发生的事情，而且按照定义，在世界各地都发生过，这就是我们为此做好准备的原因。” 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间点击此处并点击“星标”或“首选”按钮，将我们选为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

title.en: Deadly H5 strain of bird flu has been confirmed in Australia — here's what it means
title.zh: 致命H5禽流感病毒株在澳大利亚确诊——这意味着什么

summary.en: Australia has confirmed its first case of the deadly H5N1 avian influenza, a significant development for the nation's public health.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚已确认首例致命H5N1禽流感病例，这对该国的公共卫生而言是一个重大进展。

body.en:
For years, as cases of the deadly H5 strain of bird influenza wreaked havoc among animal populations across the globe, Australia had been the sole continent to avoid it successfully — until now.

On Saturday, the first positive case of the virus on the Australian mainland was confirmed.

Agriculture minister Julie Collins confirmed at a press conference in Canberra that the H5 bird flu was detected in a migratory bird in Western Australia.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Australia will do all it can to curb any spread of H5N1 bird flu.

"There's no evidence of any mass mortalities, and there's no evidence that it's in our poultry or agriculture system at this stage," Collins added.

In its efforts to tackle previous bird-flu outbreaks, Australia has tightened biosecurity measures at farms, tested shore birds for disease, vaccinated vulnerable species, and war-gamed response plans for an H5N1 outbreak.

A single migratory wild seabird potentially infected with the disease was found in Western Australia on 14 June.

Before the suspected positive case was confirmed, Collins said on Friday that it would be "not unexpected" to discover.

"This will be sobering, but not unexpected given the spread globally," she said.

The bird was a brown skua — a sub-Antarctic species — that was found on a remote beach at the Cape Le Grand National Park near Esperance, about 700km southeast of Perth.

WA Agriculture and Food Minister Jackie Jarvis said the bird was isolated after it was discovered in an unwell state on Sunday and died that night.

"I'm told it is not normal for them to be on the south coast of Western Australia," Jarvis said.

"But I am also told it's not uncommon if a bird is sick to actually be sort of blown off course, as it were."

Initial tests were confirmed overnight by the CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness.

Senior lecturer at the Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies at the University of Tasmania, Dr Jane Younger, said the species infected with the virus could give clues to its origin.

"The species involved are important," she said, noting that they are Southern Ocean and sub-Antarctic birds.

This suggests that the virus "probably reached mainland Australia through Southern Ocean wildlife movements, rather than through the northern hemisphere route we have been watching closely," Younger explained.

But, she says, genetic analysis was still essential to identify the virus' origin and whether it was linked to current outbreaks across the Southern Ocean.

title.en: German journalist detained in Syria back home, lawyer says
title.zh: 律师称在叙利亚被拘留的德国记者已回国

summary.en: Eva Maria Michelmann, a German journalist who disappeared in Syria in January during clashes between government forces and Kurdish fighters, has safely returned home, her lawyer confirmed. The German government had previously stated its efforts to secure her release.
summary.zh: 德国记者伊娃·玛丽亚·米歇尔曼已安全回国，其律师证实了这一消息。她于一月份在叙利亚失踪，当时政府军正在向叙利亚东北部的库尔德武装推进。德国政府上周曾表示正在努力让她回家。

title.en: Lebanon: Is US-Iran peace deal a 'victory' for Hezbollah?
title.zh: 黎巴嫩：美伊和平协议是真主党的“胜利”吗？

summary.en: Lebanon's Hezbollah group has claimed that the US-Iran peace deal is a "great victory." The group, which is opposed to Israel, has certainly been bolstered by the deal. But what have they really won?
summary.zh: 黎巴嫩真主党声称，美伊和平协议是其“巨大胜利”。这个反对以色列的组织无疑因该协议而受到鼓舞。但他们真正赢得了什么？

body.en:
Lebanon's Hezbollah group has claimed that the US-Iran peace deal is a "great victory." The group, which is opposed to Israel, has certainly been bolstered by the deal. But what has Hezbollah really won?

"A great victory" and a "pivotal point for Lebanon" — that was how Naim Kassem, the leader of Lebanese group Hezbollah , described on Wednesday the memorandum of understanding that stopped fighting between Iran and the United States  this week.

Kassem also thanked the Iranians for "linking the Lebanese arena" to the deal and "forcing Israel to stop its aggression."

Hezbollah was founded in 1982 with support from Iran, and one of its primary aims then was to end Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon. It has both a military and political wing and the support of much of Lebanon's Shiite Muslim community. Today, it plays a major part in Lebanese society and politics, has often been described as a "state within a state," and remains opposed to Israel. Since Kassem's comments, fighting has continued in southern Lebanon, with Hezbollah targeting Israeli soldiers and Israel continuing to destroy southern villages and use bombs and drones. Sixty days of talks between the United States and Iran, during which details would be hammered out, were scheduled to start in Switzerland on Friday, but were postponed in the morning because of Iran's opposition to the fighting in Lebanon.

Yet, despite it's troubled start, analysts say that the deal  on the table favors Hezbollah's allies in Tehran. 

"This memorandum of understanding virtually gives Iran everything it wanted and Trump everything he had [before attacking Iran, together with Israel, in February]," says James M. Dorsey, an expert on the region at Singapore's Rajaratnam School of International Studies. "And certainly, at least initially, it looks like a victory for Hezbollah."

The first paragraph of the memorandum states that the US, Iran and allies will declare an "immediate and permanent" termination of military operations on "all fronts," including Lebanon.

The deal, signed by the US, Iran and mediator Pakistan on Wednesday, also says that both will ensure "the territorial integrity and sovereignty" of Lebanon .

Israel currently occupies around 600 square kilometers in southern Lebanon and calls this a necessary "security buffer zone" needed to protect citizens in northern Israel from Hezbollah rockets. Critics of Israel say it is an invasion and occupation.

title.en: For women in China frustrated by sexism, female comics are offering a release

summary.en: Standup comedy in China is providing a platform for women to discuss sensitive topics, including sexism, offering a sense of release and shared experience. Performers, however, remain cautious of censorship limits as they navigate this space in venues like a small performing arts theatre in east Beijing.
summary.zh: 中国的脱口秀喜剧为女性提供了一个平台，让她们可以讨论包括性别歧视在内的敏感话题，从而获得宣泄和共同的体验。然而，表演者们在北京东部一家小型表演艺术剧院等场所进行表演时，仍对审查限制保持警惕。

body.en: Standup comedy gives women a space to talk about certain topics that have become more sensitive, while performers remain wary of censorship limits Packed into the upstairs theatre of a small performing arts space in east Beijing, more than 100 people, mostly women, are giddy with anticipation. “Who did you come to see?” asks the MC, fashionably dressed in a faded denim two-piece suit. The answer is bellowed in unison back to him: “Fang Zhuren!” Fang Shaoli, AKA Director Fang ( Fang Zhuren ), has built a cult following in China in the past two years. Decidedly less fashionable than the evening’s host, Fang is dressed in a yellow hoodie and dark blue jeans. Her everywoman attire is part of the appeal. With a stout frame and short, sensible haircut, Fang, who was born in 1975, hails from rural part of east China’s Shandong province. Before discovering the art of standup comedy she worked in factories and on construction sites, but mainly lived as a housewife to a difficult husband. Her jokes riff on the deep sexism that permeates Chinese culture, particularly away from the big urban centres like Beijing and Shanghai. Continue reading...
body.zh: 单口喜剧为女性提供了谈论某些变得更加敏感的话题的空间，而表演者们仍然对审查制度的限制保持警惕北京东部一个小型表演艺术空间的楼上剧场里，有 100 多人（其中大部分是女性）满怀期待。 “你是来看谁的？”身穿褪色牛仔两件套西装的主持人问道。对方齐声喊道：“方主任！”方绍立，又名方主任（方主任），过去两年在中国建立了一批狂热的追随者。方穿着黄色连帽衫和深蓝色牛仔裤，明显不如当晚主持人时尚。她的普通女性着装是其吸引力的一部分。方出生于1975年，来自中国东部山东省的农村地区，身材魁梧，留着一头漂亮的短发。在发现单口喜剧艺术之前，她曾在工厂和建筑工地工作过，但主要是作为一位难相处的丈夫的家庭主妇生活。她的笑话反复提及了渗透在中国文化中的根深蒂固的性别歧视，尤其是在远离北京和上海等大城市中心的地方。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the human need to express frustrations and experiences, especially when facing societal pressures like sexism. Proverbs 31:8-9 reminds us of the importance of speaking up for those whose voices are often unheard, advocating for justice and dignity. Even in challenging environments, creative expression can offer a vital space for shared...
reflection.zh: 这个故事突显了人类表达挫折和经历的需求，尤其是在面对性别歧视等社会压力时。箴言31:8-9提醒我们，为那些常常被忽视的声音发声，倡导公义和尊严是何等重要。即使在充满挑战的环境中，创造性的表达也能为共同的理解和释放提供一个重要的空间，这反映了雅伟对边缘群体的关怀。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Border Force officer and Hong Kong trade official jailed for spying for China
title.zh: 英国边境部队官员和香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动被判入狱

summary.en: A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official have been sentenced to 10 and eight years in prison, respectively, after being convicted of spying for China. These are the first convictions under the UK's National Security Act.
summary.zh: 一名英国边境部队官员和一名香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，刑期分别为10年和8年。这是英国根据《国家安全法》首次定罪的案件。

body.en: Peter Wai and Bill Yuen sentenced to 10 and eight years at Old Bailey in first convictions under National Security Act A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official based in London have been jailed for spying for China in the first such conviction in British criminal history. Peter Wai, who conducted “shadow policing” operations on Chinese dissidents in the UK, was sentenced to 10 years, while his handler, Bill Yuen, received an eight-year term. Continue reading...
body.zh: Peter Wai和Bill Yuen根据《国家安全法》首次在老贝利被判刑10年和8年。一名英国边防部队官员和一名驻伦敦的香港贸易官员因为中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，这是英国犯罪史上的首次此类定罪。在英国对中国持不同政见者进行“影子警察”行动的韦彼得被判处10年徒刑，而他的经纪人袁比尔则被判处8年徒刑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights the profound breach of trust when public officials betray their duties. Yahweh's word reminds us that faithfulness in small responsibilities reflects our character in larger ones. May we all strive for integrity in every role we are given, understanding that honesty builds trust and strengthens the fabric of society.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了公职人员背叛职责时对信任的严重破坏。雅伟的话语提醒我们，在小事上忠心的人，在大事上也忠心。愿我们都在所担任的每一个角色中追求正直，明白诚实能建立信任并巩固社会结构。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
verse.textZh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心；在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

title.en: Inspired by Ukraine, and worried by China: Taiwan teaches its citizens how to fly drones
title.zh: 受乌克兰启发，担忧中国大陆：台湾教导市民如何驾驶无人机

summary.en: Ordinary citizens in Taiwan are enrolling in drone piloting courses, inspired by events in Ukraine and concerned about a potential military threat from China. These courses teach participants, young and old, how to operate drones for various purposes.
summary.zh: 受乌克兰局势的启发并担忧中国大陆的军事威胁，台湾普通民众（包括年轻人和老年人）正在参加无人机驾驶课程。这些课程旨在教授学员如何操作无人机以应对潜在情况。

body.en: Ordinary Taiwanese, young and old, are joining courses to learn how to fly drones amid looming China military threat In a small, crowded room in Taipei, Pan Chien-chin is trying to keep a drone hovering steadily. Imagining himself flying a plane, he gently nudges controller joysticks to guide the insect-like device as it hums through the air. Cheers break out as Pan, who has never flown a drone before, steers it around a rectangular course marked by traffic cones without crashing. Around him are about two dozen fellow trainees, all signed up for the same course: Taiwan’s first civil defence drone training programme. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾普通民众，无论老少，都在参加课程，学习如何在迫在眉睫的中国军事威胁下驾驶无人机。在台北一间拥挤的小房间里，潘建钦正努力让无人机保持稳定盘旋。他想象自己驾驶一架飞机，轻轻推动控制器操纵杆，引导昆虫般的设备在空中嗡嗡作响。当潘以前从未驾驶过无人机时，他驾驶无人机绕着一个由交通锥标标记的矩形航线飞行，没有坠毁，引发了欢呼声。他周围大约有两打学员，他们都报名参加同一门课程：台湾首个民防无人机训练计划。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The story highlights a community's proactive response to perceived threats, reflecting a natural human inclination to prepare for potential dangers. Proverbs reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing trouble and taking steps to protect ourselves and our communities. Such foresight, when coupled with a reliance on Yahweh, can guide us in uncertain times.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻讲述了一个社区如何积极应对潜在威胁，反映了人类为可能出现的危险做准备的自然倾向。箴言提醒我们，预见祸患并采取措施保护自己和社区是智慧之举。这种远见，若能与对雅伟的信靠结合，便能在不确定的时期指引我们。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Lululemon apologises after Japanese drum row at Great Wall yoga event
title.zh: Lululemon因长城瑜伽活动中的日本太鼓风波致歉

summary.en: The activewear brand Lululemon issued an apology after an online uproar in China. The controversy stemmed from a promotional yoga event held on the Great Wall of China, where a Japanese taiko drum was mistakenly featured instead of a Chinese drum, despite the event being intended to celebrate Chinese culture.
summary.zh: 运动服饰品牌Lululemon因在中国长城举办的瑜伽推广活动中误用日本太鼓而引发网络争议后，发表了道歉声明。尽管该活动旨在庆祝中国文化，但这一失误在中国引发了线上轩然大波。

body.en: Online uproar follows Canadian brand’s use of taiko drum at sponsored festival held to celebrate Chinese culture The activewear brand Lululemon has apologised after a promotional event held on the Great Wall of China appeared to mistakenly feature a Japanese drum, prompting an uproar. The Canadian-headquartered company, known for its upmarket leggings, has been growing rapidly in China and arranged for a yoga festival to take place in late May on a section of the wall near Beijing. Continue reading...
body.zh: 加拿大品牌在为庆祝中国文化而举办的赞助节日上使用太鼓，在中国引起网络轩然大波运动服品牌 Lululemon 在中国长城举行的一次促销活动中错误地使用了日本太鼓，引发轩然大波，该品牌已道歉。这家总部位于加拿大的公司以其高档瑜伽紧身裤而闻名，在中国发展迅速，并于五月底在北京附近的一段长城举办了一场瑜伽节。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This incident reminds us how quickly a seemingly small cultural misstep can ignite widespread public sentiment, especially in the digital age. Just as a tiny spark can set a vast forest ablaze, unintentional actions or symbols can inadvertently cause significant uproar and division. It underscores the need for careful consideration and humility in our...
reflection.zh: 这起事件提醒我们，一个看似微小的文化失误，尤其在数字时代，能多么迅速地引发广泛的公众情绪。正如一点火花能点燃整片森林，无意的行为或象征也可能不经意间造成巨大的争议和分歧。这强调了我们在互动中需要谨慎思考和谦卑，认识到即使是微小的细节也可能产生深远的影响。

verse.textEn: The tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark.
verse.textZh: 舌头在百体里也是最小的，却能说大话。看哪，最小的火能点着最大的树林。

title.en: They were forced into marriage and abused. Now women facing exploitation in China have a glimmer of hope
title.zh: 她们被迫结婚并遭受虐待。现在，中国面临剥削的女性有了一线希望

summary.en: Female activists are secretly working to locate and assist vulnerable women in China who have been forced into marriage and subjected to abuse, as they believe authorities are not adequately protecting them.
summary.zh: 在中国，女性活动家们正在秘密寻找并帮助那些被迫结婚并遭受虐待的弱势女性，因为她们担心官方未能提供足够的保护。

body.en: Female activists are working in the shadows to find and support vulnerable women they fear are being failed by authorities Last summer, Xiaocao, a softly spoken woman in her 40s, received a tip-off that in Lüliang, a small city in China’s Shanxi province, vulnerable women were being forced into marriages. Along with another volunteer, she wanted to investigate. After leaving Beijing, the two volunteers travelled south for hours, on trains and in rental cars. A few villages turned out to be dead ends. But on the final day of their trip, the women stopped in a county where they’d heard about a woman with learning disabilities who was “married” to two brothers. Soon, they found her. Continue reading...
body.zh: 女性活动人士正在暗中寻找和支持她们担心当局辜负的弱势女性。去年夏天，40 多岁、说话轻声细语的小曹接到举报，称在中国山西省的一个小城市吕梁，弱势女性正在被迫结婚。她想和另一名志愿者一起进行调查。离开北京后，两名志愿者乘坐火车和租车向南行驶了几个小时。一些村庄变成了死胡同。但在旅行的最后一天，妇女们在一个县停下来，她们听说那里有一名有学习障碍的妇女“嫁给”了两个兄弟。很快，他们就找到了她。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the courageous work of activists who step in when vulnerable individuals are failed by systems meant to protect them. Their efforts embody the call to speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, advocating for justice and dignity for the exploited.
reflection.zh: 这个故事彰显了活动家们的勇气，当弱势群体未能得到应有的保护时，她们挺身而出。她们的努力体现了为那些无法为自己发声的人说话的呼召，为受剥削者争取正义和尊严。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: The Guardian view on the global baby bust: people are having fewer children – even where they say they want more | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》观点：全球生育率暴跌——人们生育的孩子越来越少，即使他们说想要更多 | 社论

summary.en: A new report indicates that global fertility rates are falling faster and spreading further than anticipated, with India's fertility now below the level needed for population stability. This trend means that two-thirds of the world's population now lives in countries with declining birth rates.
summary.zh: 一份新报告指出，全球生育率下降的速度和范围都超出了预期，印度生育率已降至维持人口稳定所需的水平以下。这一趋势意味着全球三分之二的人口生活在生育率下降的国家。

body.en: Indian fertility has fallen below the rate required for population stability, in further evidence of the unexpectedly rapid decline in births internationally The global fall in fertility rates has arrived faster and spread further than anticipated. Two-thirds of people now live in countries that have slipped below the replacement rate – 2.1 births per woman – required for a stable population. Last month, India revealed that its fertility rate had fallen to just 1.9 . The world’s two most populous nations, which pursued cruel and coercive policies to cut births, both face shrinking populations. China’s fertility rate is now around 1, and births last year fell below 8 million – just over half the number projected when the “one child” policy was axed 10 years ago, and comparable to the total in 1738, when its population was 150 million. It’s further proof that what was seen as a phenomenon of rich nations has spread far beyond them. East Asia led the way. But Albania and Chile have far lower rates than the US or England and Wales (themselves experiencing record lows of 1.6 and 1.4). Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...
body.zh: 印度的生育率已降至人口稳定所需的水平以下，这进一步证明了国际上出生率出人意料地迅速下降。全球生育率下降的速度和蔓延范围都超出了预期。目前，三分之二的人口生活在人口更替率（每名妇女生育 2.1 胎）以下的国家。上个月，印度透露其生育率已降至仅 1.9。世界上两个人口最多的国家都推行残酷和强制性的政策来减少生育，但都面临着人口萎缩的问题。目前中国的生育率约为1，去年的出生人数跌至800万以下——仅略高于10年前取消“独生子女”政策时预计数字的一半，与1738年的总人口相当，当时的人口为1.5亿。这进一步证明，被视为富裕国家现象的现象已经远远超出了它们的范围。东亚处于领先地位。但阿尔巴尼亚和智利的利率远低于美国或英格兰和威尔士（它们自己也经历过 1.6 和 1.4 的历史低点）。您对本文提出的问题有什么看法吗？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The global decline in birth rates highlights a significant shift in societal patterns regarding family and future generations. Psalm 127:3 reminds us that children are a heritage from Yahweh, a reward and a blessing that enrich life and carry hope for the future. This perspective invites reflection on the profound value of each new life.
reflection.zh: 全球生育率下降的趋势，反映了社会在家庭和未来世代模式上的重大转变。诗篇127:3提醒我们，儿女是雅伟所赐的产业，是祂所给的赏赐，他们丰富生命，承载着未来的希望。这一视角邀请我们反思每个新生命的深远价值。

verse.textEn: Children are a heritage from Yahweh, offspring a reward from him.
verse.textZh: 儿女是雅伟所赐的产业。

title.en: From camel coats to guochao: Max Mara woos China’s luxury brand consumers
title.zh: 从骆驼绒大衣到国潮：Max Mara如何吸引中国奢侈品消费者

summary.en: Luxury fashion brand Max Mara celebrated its 75th anniversary with a catwalk show in Shanghai, paying tribute to Chinese style to attract consumers in China's growing luxury market.
summary.zh: 奢侈时尚品牌Max Mara在上海举办了75周年时装秀，以中国风情致敬当地文化，旨在吸引中国日益增长的奢侈品市场消费者。

body.en: Fashion house pays tribute to Chinese style with its 75th anniversary catwalk show in Shanghai “New York may be the city that never sleeps, but Shanghai doesn’t even sit down.” For the British designer Ian Griffiths, who encountered this line in the New Yorker, it summed up why China’s biggest city was the right place to celebrate Max Mara’s 75th anniversary. “Max Mara is a product for metropolitan women, and it would be patronising to assume that a metropolitan wardrobe should be western-centric,” Griffiths said. Continue reading...
body.zh: 时装屋在上海举办 75 周年时装秀，向中国风致敬 “纽约可能是不夜城，但上海却从不坐下。”对于在《纽约客》上看到这句话的英国设计师 Ian Griffiths 来说，它总结了为什么中国最大的城市是庆祝 Max Mara 75 周年的最佳地点。 “Max Mara 是一款专为都市女性设计的产品，如果认为都市女性的衣橱应该以西方为中心，那就太居高临下了，”Griffiths 说道。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The allure of luxury fashion and the relentless pursuit of market share highlight the powerful draw of material wealth and worldly success. This story invites us to consider where our ultimate devotion lies, reminding us that our hearts cannot be fully given to both God and the pursuit of riches.
reflection.zh: 奢华时尚的魅力和对市场份额的孜孜不倦，凸显了物质财富和世俗成功的强大吸引力。这个故事邀请我们思考我们最终的忠诚所在，提醒我们不能同时全心全意地侍奉雅伟和追求财富。

verse.textEn: No one can serve two masters... You cannot serve both God and Mammon.
verse.textZh: 一个人不能事奉两个主……你们不能又事奉神，又事奉玛门。

title.en: US military plans major war stockpile on Australian soil
title.zh: 美国军方计划在澳大利亚建立大型战争储备

summary.en: The United States military is planning a significant accumulation of weapons on Australian territory. This move is described as a key part of an Asia-wide regional defense strategy aimed at countering the growing influence of China.
summary.zh: 美国军方正计划在澳大利亚领土上大量储备武器。此举被描述为一项旨在对抗中国崛起势力的亚洲区域防御战略的关键组成部分。

body.en:
The US military is planning a permanent war-ready weapons stockpile for its marine corps on Australia's southeast coast beyond the range of most Chinese missiles, tender documents show and officials confirmed to the Agence France-Presse news agency (AFP).

The development of the stockpile, a first for the US marine corps in Australia, comes as the United States is keen to leverage the continent's strategic location in the South Pacific to counter China's rapid military build-up, analysts said.

The US marine corps began global prepositioning of military supplies during the Cold War — using floating stores on ships and caves in Norway where weapons, ammunition and vehicles to sustain thousands of troops are kept.

The first land stockpile in the Asia-Pacific region is expected to open this year in the Philippines, close to potential flashpoints in the South China Sea.

Documents published by the US navy this month show advanced planning for an even larger Australian stockpile, with US$30 million ($42.4M) allocated to build warehouses and offices in southeastern Victoria state for "critical forward provisioning".

The Australian stockpile, expected to reach full capacity by 2028, will be kept in Melbourne before being moved to US warehouses to be constructed next year at an Australian military base at Bandiana in rural Victoria, tender documents show.

Australia does not permit foreign military bases on its soil, a sensitive issue in a country that has a security alliance with the United States and is hosting an increasing variety of US forces on rotation at Australian defence bases.

The US navy is engaging a global defence contractor to employ around 110 engineers, mechanics, material and safety specialists to manage the Australian stockpile, which includes "crew-served weapons", the documents show.

"Marine corps activities in Australia support integrated global sustainment by maintaining ready-for-issue equipment and supplies for operations and exercises across the Indo-Pacific," a US marine corps forces pacific spokesperson told AFP.

The spokesperson declined to comment on contract details or force planning assumptions but said marines' equipment is kept at "high readiness".

Contracting arrangements and the operation of the facility would be made in close coordination with Australia's Department of Defence.

"These activities improve responsiveness, strengthen interoperability with allies and partners, and support a range of missions across the Indo-Pacific," the spokesperson said, using an alternative description for the Asia-Pacific region.

title.en: Charging ahead: EVs outpace growth predictions
title.zh: 电动汽车：超越增长预期，加速前进

summary.en: Electric vehicles are becoming more affordable, efficient, and capable of longer distances, exceeding initial growth forecasts. China is leading this transition, with Europe and other nations rapidly advancing as well.
summary.zh: 电动汽车正变得更便宜、更高效，续航里程也比以往任何时候都长，其增长速度超出了预期。中国正在推动这一转型，而欧洲和其他国家也正在迅速追赶。

body.zh: 电动汽车变得越来越便宜、越来越高效，而且行驶距离比以往任何时候都更远。中国正在推动这一转型，但欧洲和其他国家正在快速追赶。 全球电动汽车 (EV) 市场的增长速度远远快于预期。短短六年内，销量增长了十倍，到 2025 年，全球电动汽车销量将达到约 2100 万辆。 中国和欧洲处于领先地位，但世界其他地区的市场也在快速增长。 中国长期以来一直在投资太阳能和风能以及电池技术——电动汽车最关键的组成部分。 得益于先进的研究和大规模生产，电动汽车电池成本大幅下降。如今，它们的成本仅为 10 年前的四分之一，而且价格还在继续下降。 中国是世界上最大的汽车市场，消费者正在从政府的产业战略中获益。自 2024 年以来，电动汽车的成本低于内燃机汽车，国家多年来一直在迅速扩大充电基础设施，而且中国的电力非常实惠。 2015年，电动汽车仅占中国新车销量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，这一比例已攀升至 61%。 电动汽车依靠电力运行并通过电缆充电。在全球范围内，三分之二的电动汽车是所谓的电池电动汽车 (BEV)，仅由电力驱动。剩下的三分之一还配备了燃气发动机，用于长途旅行时的备用——这些被称为增程电动汽车 (EREV) 或插电式混合动力电动汽车 (PHEV)。 相比之下，所谓的混合动力电动汽车 (HEV) 始终需要汽油或柴油来为其内燃机提供动力。电动机提供一些帮助，仅通过再生制动产生电力。这项技术在一定程度上降低了城市驾驶的燃油消耗，但混合动力汽车在国际统计中并未被算作电动汽车。 2018年，电动汽车仅占欧盟新车注册量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，售出的新车中近三分之一是电动汽车。 北欧处于领先地位。在挪威，现在销售的几乎所有新车都是电动汽车（99%），其次是丹麦（82%）和瑞典（65%）。该地区各国政府支持气候友好型出行，并正在扩大充电基础设施。 在英国，2026 年 4 月注册的新车中有 39% 是电动汽车，其次是德国（37%）和法国（32%）。在这三个国家，电动汽车销量与去年同月相比都翻了一番。 近年来，美国市场陷入停滞。 2023 年至 2025 年间，电动汽车占...

title.en: Girlfriends review – love and growing pains in queer coming-of-age tale that goes from Hong Kong to Taiwan
title.zh: 女朋友》影评：一部从香港到台湾的酷儿成长故事，充满爱与成长的烦恼

summary.en: The film "Girlfriends" is a romantic drama by Tracy Choi, following one woman's journey from high school to her mid-30s, exploring love and the challenges of growing up within a queer coming-of-age narrative set between Hong Kong and Taiwan.
summary.zh: 电影《女朋友》是崔允信执导的一部浪漫剧情片，讲述了一名女性从高中到三十多岁的人生旅程，探讨了在香港和台湾之间发生的酷儿成长故事中的爱与成长烦恼。

body.en: A trio of actors play one woman from high school to her mid-30s in Tracy Choi’s thoughtful romantic drama It can stretch credibility a little when an actor plays the same character over a long time span in one film. Richard Linklater solved the problem in Boyhood by shooting scenes over succeeding years; AI and de-ageing effects are now an option. With this intimate queer coming-of-age drama, film-maker Tracy Choi instead casts a trio of actors to play one woman from high school to her mid-30s. The three don’t look particularly alike; their temperaments overlap but are by no means identical. The point is perhaps to show how intense the transitions into adulthood are, how unrecognisable are the people we used to be. Working backwards, Girlfriends begins in Hong Kong, where 34-year-old film director Lok (Fish Liew) lives with her actor girlfriend Bei (Jennifer Yu). Five years earlier, Choi released a feature film, but her career has stalled. She is directionless and restless. Bei is also applying pressure to buy a flat and have a baby. The film then rewinds 12 years, to Taiwan, when Lok was a student with spiky orange hair, known as Choi (played by Elizabeth Tang). Some of the best scenes in the film come when her parents visit from Macau; Choi and her girlfriend Qing (Han Ning) have been pretending to be flatmates. Then, as the four of them eat dinner one night, unwilling to keep up the charade, Choi grabs Qing’s hand fiercely over the dinner table. She is coming out to her parents; they understand but say nothing. Another film might give us a big showdown, but this is probably how it would have happened in real life. Continue reading...
body.zh: 在 Tracy Choi 这部深思熟虑的浪漫剧中，三位演员扮演一名从高中到 30 多岁的女性。当一个演员在一部电影中长时间扮演同一个角色时，可信度会有所提高。理查德·林克莱特在《少年时代》中通过连续几年拍摄场景解决了这个问题。人工智能和抗衰老效果现在是一种选择。在这部亲密的酷儿成长剧中，电影制片人崔西·崔 (Tracy Choi) 聘请了三名演员来扮演一名从高中到 30 多岁的女性。这三个人看起来并不是特别相似。他们的性格有重叠，但绝不相同。重点也许是为了表明向成年的转变是多么激烈，我们过去的样子是多么难以辨认。时光倒流，《女朋友》的故事发生在香港，34 岁的电影导演乐（刘静茹饰）和她的演员女友贝（余珍妮饰）住在一起。五年前，崔发布了一部故事片，但她的事业却陷入了停滞。她没有方向，焦躁不安。贝还施加压力，要求买一套公寓并生孩子。影片随后将时间倒回12年前的台湾，当时乐还是一名留着尖尖橙色头发的学生，名叫崔（伊丽莎白·唐饰）。影片中一些最精彩的场景出现在她的父母从澳门来访时；崔和女友青（韩宁饰）一直假装是室友。然后，有一天晚上，当他们四个人吃晚饭时，崔不愿继续玩这个游戏，在餐桌上猛烈地抓住了庆的手。她向父母出柜了；他们明白但什么也没说。另一部电影可能会给我们带来一场大对决，但这可能就是现实生活中发生的情况。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This film explores the complex journey of self-discovery and relationships, highlighting the universal human experience of love and growing pains. In every person's unique path of identity and connection, we are reminded of the profound truth that each individual is created in the image of God, possessing inherent dignity and worth.
reflection.zh: 这部电影探讨了自我发现和关系的复杂旅程，突显了爱与成长烦恼的普世人性体验。在每个人独特的身份和联结之路上，我们都被提醒着一个深刻的真理：每个人都是按照雅伟的形象被创造的，拥有固有的尊严和价值。

title.en: What's next for the Socceroos?
title.zh: 澳大利亚国家足球队何去何从？

summary.en: After a crushing loss to the USA, the Socceroos will have one more shot to qualify for the next round.
summary.zh: 在惨败给美国队之后，澳大利亚国家足球队将有最后一次机会争取晋级下一轮。

body.en:
Socceroos and their fans around the world are reeling after a crushing loss to the USA on Saturday.

The shocking defeat began in the tenth minute with an own goal from Australia and ended with the Stars and Stripes closing in for a 2-0 win.

The result has sent Aussies careening back down to earth from the high pedestal set by the national team's 2-0 victory against Türkiye less than a week ago.

Socceroos coach Tony Popovic's selection decisions have come under scrutiny after the heartbreaking loss — Nestory Irankunda and Conor Metcalfe were benched in the opening half against the USA despite both players scoring against Türkiye in the team's opening match.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Popovic admitted the Socceroos looked "sluggish" and "heavy-legged" on Saturday, but said he didn't think the starting personnel would have made much of a difference against the USA's forceful performance.

"They were quicker, they were more powerful. They won every duel, they won every second ball, and when you do that, it makes it very difficult," he said.

But while humbling, it's far from the end for the Socceroos. Saturday's loss may mean the USA has topped Group D and will advance to the next round, the Group of 32, but Australia could still qualify with a second or third-place finish.

Saturday would prove consequential not only for Australia, but also for Türkiye, which became the second nation after Haiti to be eliminated from the 2026 World Cup after it was defeated by Paraguay 0-1. After this match, Paraguay levelled up to third place, where it is now equal with Australia on three points.

Australia will play Paraguay next week at 12pm on Friday, 26 June (AEST) at Santa Clara, near San Francisco, with the Socceroos needing just a win or a draw to progress automatically in second spot.

And automatic progression to the Group of 32 in second place would see Australia compete against another runner-up team, likely in Group G. In that group, the favourite pick to win is Belgium, while New Zealand, Iran and Egypt are battling for second place.

If Australia loses against Paraguay, it can still qualify for the Round of 32 as one of the best third-placed teams. This is because the top two teams from each group will advance to the Group of 32, along with the eight best third-place teams. A total of 32 teams will play in these knockout stages — you lose once, and you are out for good.

If the Socceroos made it to the Group of 32 under these conditions, their first match would be against a major group winner.

Paraguay's win cements the USA at the top of their group, a feat the team has only achieved twice, in 1930 and 2010....

title.en: Fears doctors criticising Israel may be silenced as health watchdog adopts contested antisemitism definition

title.en: From nightclubs and worksites, fans in Sydney and Melbourne gathered before dawn to cheer on the Socceroos

body.en: Energised by a surprise victory over Turkey, people gathered at 5am in every capital city on Saturday, some having pulled all-nighters Australians gathered in their thousands before sunrise, holding babies, heading home from nightclubs or heading off to work, to watch the Socceroos face off against the US. title.en: Police 'disappointed' following football fan chaos at watch events
title.zh: 警方对球迷观赛活动中的混乱表示“失望”

summary.en: Arrests were made at fan sites in both Sydney and Melbourne on Friday morning following incidents of disorder during football watch events, leading police to express disappointment.

body.en:
Victorian police have said that flares and fireworks were "disappointingly" set off by football fans gathered at Federation Square for the Australia-United States match on Saturday morning.

Arrests were made at fan sites in the Victorian capital as well as Sydney's Tumbalong Park, where thousands of Socceroos fans packed in to watch the event in the early hours.

One man was treated at the scene in Sydney for facial burns after being hit in the face by a flare.

In Melbourne, mounted police were forced to intervene after fans attempted to breach barriers at Fed Square when the popular site reached capacity just after 4am on Saturday.

About 7,500 fans packed the site in cold and rainy conditions, with 14 flares and one firework set off before the match, leading to two arrests.

Fed Square said they would review Friday's operations with Victoria Police and apply any learnings to future screenings.

"We will continue working closely with police and other stakeholders to ensure the safest possible experience for everyone attending Federation Square," they said.

While fans celebrated the atmosphere, there was disappointment as the Socceroos' campaign suffered a setback with a 2-0 loss to the American team.

Former Socceroo Craig Foster, who was the MC at the live site, urged fans to stop letting off flares.

A 16-year-old boy was also arrested in relation to an alleged sexual assault of a woman about 4.55am.

Almost 9000 eager fans were redirected to AAMI Park, where the match was also livestreamed.

Sydney experienced similarly fiery scenes with two men, aged 20, arrested at Tumbarong Park in the city centre and later charged with possessing a bright light distress signal in a public place.

title.en: Deadly H5 strain of bird flu has been confirmed in Australia — here's what it means
title.zh: 致命H5禽流感病毒株在澳大利亚确诊——这意味着什么

summary.en: Australia has confirmed its first case of the deadly H5N1 avian influenza, a significant development for the nation's public health.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚已确认首例致命H5N1禽流感病例，这对该国的公共卫生而言是一个重大进展。

body.en:
For years, as cases of the deadly H5 strain of bird influenza wreaked havoc among animal populations across the globe, Australia had been the sole continent to avoid it successfully — until now.

On Saturday, the first positive case of the virus on the Australian mainland was confirmed.

Agriculture minister Julie Collins confirmed at a press conference in Canberra that the H5 bird flu was detected in a migratory bird in Western Australia.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Australia will do all it can to curb any spread of H5N1 bird flu.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"There's no evidence of any mass mortalities, and there's no evidence that it's in our poultry or agriculture system at this stage," Collins added.

In its efforts to tackle previous bird-flu outbreaks, Australia has tightened biosecurity measures at farms, tested shore birds for disease, vaccinated vulnerable species, and war-gamed response plans for an H5N1 outbreak.

A single migratory wild seabird potentially infected with the disease was found in Western Australia on 14 June.

Before the suspected positive case was confirmed, Collins said on Friday that it would be "not unexpected" to discover.

"This will be sobering, but not unexpected given the spread globally," she said.

The bird was a brown skua — a sub-Antarctic species — that was found on a remote beach at the Cape Le Grand National Park near Esperance, about 700km southeast of Perth.

WA Agriculture and Food Minister Jackie Jarvis said the bird was isolated after it was discovered in an unwell state on Sunday and died that night.

"I'm told it is not normal for them to be on the south coast of Western Australia," Jarvis said.

"But I am also told it's not uncommon if a bird is sick to actually be sort of blown off course, as it were."

Initial tests were confirmed overnight by the CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness.

Senior lecturer at the Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies at the University of Tasmania, Dr Jane Younger, said the species infected with the virus could give clues to its origin.

"The species involved are important," she said, noting that they are Southern Ocean and sub-Antarctic birds.

This suggests that the virus "probably reached mainland Australia through Southern Ocean wildlife movements, rather than through the northern hemisphere route we have been watching closely," Younger explained.

But, she says, genetic analysis was still essential to identify the virus' origin and whether it was linked to current outbreaks across the Southern Ocean.

body.en:
The USA's dominant display proved too much for the Socceroos in Seattle with Australia going down 2-0, but still with a solid chance to progress to the next round of the FIFA World Cup.

The Socceroos defence that held so well against Türkiye had cracks in it, as the visitors conceded both goals in the first half. The second half was a more promising display from the Socceroos with young star Nestory Irankunde coming on and helping to lift the tempo, but not enough for a goal.

Socceroos coach Tony Popovic once again chose the element of surprise for his opening lineup and some Socceroos supporters were left scratching their heads with the two goal scorers against Türkiye, Nestory Irankunda and Conor Metcalfe, starting on the bench.

Mathew Leckie, known for his heroic goal against Denmark at the 2022 World Cup, and Nishan Velupillay started in their place.

Folarin Balogun ran down the left flank, and makes a cross into the six yard box where Australian defender Cam Burgess knocked it into the back of the net.

Jordy Bos received a yellow card after a block on Weston McKennie that pushed his face early in the second half and Alessandro Circati picked up another in the 31st minute.

In the 44th minute the USA went 2-0 up after a goal that Australian fans were hoping wouldn't stand.

They won a free kick on the edge of the penalty area. It was passed to the centre, with the shot coming from Sergiño Dest. The initial shot deflected by an Australian defender, going high, before being headed in by Alex Freeman.

Both goals were unlucky — an own goal and offside goal overturned by VAR — but the USA created far more chances.

At half time, Harry Kewell, part of SBS's presenter line-up, said the Socceroos have been "not good enough".

"We're just getting the ball and kicking it long where Toure has had no chance."

Popovic didn't waste any time in the break substituting Jason Geria, Conor Metcalfe and Nestory Irankunda on as Nishan Velupillay, Cam Burgess and Mo Touré went off.

But former Socceroo and broadcasting legend Craig Foster told SBS the decision not to start Irankunda had a high cost.

"I'm not sure why, Popa kept Irankunda on the bench, given that he was so brilliant in the first game. And the importance of the game against Turkiye was we went one-nil up instead of one-nil down.

"That's critical when you have a defensive style of play. So, you know, I think that decision has probably cost him. He's come on now in the second half to try and chase the game again. That's the most difficult position to be in."

body.en:
Petrol prices are at their lowest since mid-February, we've been told we may be over-estimating how much superannuation we actually need, and the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) held off on lifting interest rates this week.

That may sound like relief. But for households, there are still reasons to be cautious.

The national average for a litre of unleaded fell 5.6 cents last week to just over $1.69, according to the Australian Institute of Petroleum.

That's the lowest since mid-February, which was before the outbreak of the war in the Middle East.

It comes as the global oil price tumbled around 10 per cent this week following the unveiling of a framework to end the conflict — though negotiations are off to a shaky start .

While there are some ongoing uncertainties, the fall in oil prices should make petrol even cheaper in the coming weeks.

At the same time, the government's temporary fuel excise discount is scheduled to end , putting 26.3 cents per litre back onto the price of petrol and eating into any recent benefits.

The RBA left the cash rate unchanged at 4.35 per cent this week, delivering no immediate relief for mortgage holders.

While the decision was widely expected, the central bank's message remained cautious. Policymakers said inflation remains persistent and indicated further rate rises remain possible if price pressures do not ease as expected.

But with the economy slowing, three of the big four banks say the RBA may be done hiking interest rates, with cuts pencilled in for sometime in 2027.

We'll know more about the direction of inflation when the Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes the monthly consumer price index on Wednesday.

Many Australians may be overestimating how much they need to save for retirement.

New figures from the Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia (ASFA) show a single person retiring today needs around $630,000 in superannuation savings to fund a comfortable retirement. For a couple, that figure rises to around $730,000.

According to ASFA, a comfortable retirement includes activities and expenses many Australians would associate with a relatively active lifestyle. That includes top-level private health insurance, home internet, car ownership, regular meals out, annual domestic travel and an overseas trip every seven years.

The findings come as many Australians continue to worry about whether they're saving enough. ASFA says 42 per cent of people believe they will need more than $1 million in retirement savings.

title.en: The Afghan family who are safe at last and full of hope, thanks to an Australia Pauline Hanson will never know

summary.en: The article highlights an Afghan family who found safety and hope in Australia, contrasting their experience with the anti-immigrant rhetoric of a politician. This story emerged during International Refugee Week, showcasing different perspectives on welcoming those seeking refuge.
summary.zh: 文章讲述了一个阿富汗家庭在澳大利亚找到安全和希望的故事，并将其与一位政治家反移民的言论形成对比。这个故事在国际难民周期间出现，展示了对欢迎寻求庇护者不同的看法。

body.en:
Ben Doherty in Apollo Bay Fri 19 Jun 2026 11.00 EDT Last modified on Fri 19 Jun 2026 22.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google They came in the chill of winter to hear their speaker, a man known to most only as a name.

“Thank you,” Mohammad Ibrahim told the people of Apollo Bay. “Today I am proud to call Australia my home.”

Here, assembled before him in the Mechanics Hall, was the town that made that happen. A town that raised money so he could eat and his children could be clothed, raised hell with members of parliament, ministers, bureaucrats, journalists – anyone who would listen, and many who wouldn’t – to see that Australia upheld its obligation to him.

“Never underestimate the power of kindness,” he said. “Because what may seem like a small action to you can become the difference between hope and despair for someone else.”

During this country’s longest war in Afghanistan, Mohammad Ibrahim worked on Australia’s behalf , as an interpreter for a government-sponsored aid project in Uruzgan province.

The program built and ran schools for children in one of Afghanistan’s poorest provinces, it taught girls to read in places where few ever set foot in a classroom.

It vaccinated children who’d never visited a hospital, and trained midwives and doctors in a country with one of the highest infant mortality rates in the world.

Ibrahim was proud of the difference his work was making: “Working on those projects was an honour for me to serve my country and also help the Australian government.”

But when Afghanistan fell with terrifying swiftness to the Taliban in August 2021, Ibrahim was abandoned.

Like thousands who had believed in the mission of Republican Afghanistan, who’d trusted the promises of peace and prosperity, who’d been repeatedly assured by the countries they served they would be protected in the event of calamity, he and his family were forsaken.

International hopes for a reformed Taliban, that their desire for international legitimacy would restrain their most grotesque excesses – their brutality towards women, their violent persecution of minorities – were short-lived. The Taliban were unreformed.

In their eyes, Ibrahim was an “infidel” – a member of the Hazara ethnic and religious minority, and one who’d served the western invaders. With his young family, he was forced to flee into the mountains.

Over four long years in hiding , the family lived in caves in the highlands of Bamyan, walked over precipitous mountains to remote villages where the Taliban’s reach was limited. They also rented tiny rooms in Kabul, too afraid to go out, even to buy food, uncertain that the anonymity of the capital would be any protection.

Sometimes they had a few weeks in the same place, once a couple of months. Some days they were forced to move...

title.en: Heartbreak for Australia after 2-0 loss to USA, despite better second half — as it happened
title.zh: 澳大利亚队0比2不敌美国队，下半场表现虽有改善，仍心碎告负

summary.en: Australia's national soccer team, the Socceroos, suffered a 2-0 defeat against the USA. Coach Tony Popovic's unexpected first-half lineup proved ineffective against the American offense, despite the team's improved performance in the second half.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚国家足球队“袋鼠军团”以0比2不敌美国队。尽管下半场表现有所改善，但主教练托尼·波波维奇出人意料的上半场阵容未能抵挡住美国队的攻势。

reflection.en: A coach's strategic decisions are crucial in competitive sports, and this loss highlights how even well-intentioned plans can fall short without effective guidance. In any endeavor, seeking wise counsel and sound strategy is vital for success, reminding us that collective wisdom often provides the best path forward.
reflection.zh: 在竞技体育中，教练的战略决策至关重要；这场失利提醒我们，即使是善意的计划，若缺乏有效指导也可能功亏一篑。在任何事业中，寻求明智的建议和可靠的策略都至关重要，这提醒我们集体的智慧往往能指引最佳前进方向。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。
